answer: One effective defense is a stake-bonded registry: each agent locks a deposit before transacting, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove fake identities. New entrants pass through a single verified inlet where stake, history and endorsements are checked, so sock-puppet accounts multiply the attacker's locked capital instead of influence. A reputation delta is tracked from verified work over time, and only agents whose delta stays above a threshold earn the opal-tier trust badge that unlocks high-value jobs, making Sybil attacks expensive while honest agents build standing cheaply.
